transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2027-10-04 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood Support); Dr. Aaron Kim (CTO), Leah Torres (Head of ML), Samir Patel (DevOps), Jasmine Lee (PM)
Meeting ID: rwd-2027-10-04-skyline-onboard-001

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align goals for onboarding, clarify networking (VPC, IP allowlist), SSO and data residency questions, confirm pilot scope (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and schedule technical deep-dive. Agreed next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, welcome. Thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. I'm Maya, I'll be your CSM for the onboarding. Evan from solutions engineering is here, Jordan from support.
[00:18] Dr. Aaron: Thanks Maya. Appreciate it. We're excited to get Redwood running — we've been evaluating a couple of options and want to make sure we can hit production by Q1.
[00:30] Maya: Yep, that timeline makes sense. Today we want to cover high-level milestones, responsibilities, and the specific network / security needs so Evan can follow up with the deep technical stuff.
[00:44] Evan: Hi all. Quick note: we'll do a VPC/private deployment deep-dive next week but want to capture the initial constraints now. Samir, can you outline your infra?
[00:56] Samir: Sure. We run primarily on AWS, us-west-2. We have a managed EKS cluster for our services, and a VPN to our colo. We prefer not to expose customer data outside our VPC. We'd like Redwood to either run in our VPC or provide a private peering option.
[01:15] Evan: OK, that's good. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and on-prem in our model. There are two common patterns: one is a customer-managed VPC peering with a private control plane, the other is our dedicated tenancy in an isolated VPC with strict ingress controls. We will outline both approaches.
[01:33] Jasmine: Quick Q on compliance — do you have SOC 2 and will audit logs be available? That's critical for our compliance team.
[01:44] Maya: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We provide audit logs and activity history via the Console; we can also export logs to your SIEM. I'll send the compliance pack after this call.
[01:58] Dr. Aaron: What's the encryption story? We need customer-managed keys or an HSM option.
[02:05] Evan: We integrate with KMS and support customer-managed keys for private deployments; there is KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we use platform-managed keys but can restrict data retention.
[02:20] Leah: On data retention — we have PHI in some prompts, so we'd prefer no persistent storage of raw prompts. Is there a way to disable retention on hosted?
[02:32] Maya: We have retention controls and can implement short retention or encryption-at-rest with restricted access. For PHI we typically recommend private deployment so logs never leave your environment. We'll document the options.
[02:46] Samir: Network-wise, we'll need an allowlist of egress IPs if you host. If Redwood's hosted requires outbound peering, we need static IPs for our firewall team.
[02:58] Evan: Absolutely — we'll provide an IP allowlist. For Dedicated we can also do VPC peering so no public egress is required.
[03:12] Maya: For the pilot, to de-risk, we usually recommend starting with Hosted API in restricted retention mode to move quickly, then if the latency or policy requirements push you, move to Dedicated or Private. How does that sound?
[03:28] Dr. Aaron: Sounds reasonable. Our main concerns are latency for inference and predictable cost. Leah, did you run the model evaluation on sample prompts?
[03:39] Leah: We ran a few tests against OpenAI and an internal self-hosted Llama variant. Latency varies — sub-200ms is ideal for interactive UIs, but our key use will accept up to 500ms for batched jobs. We'll share the prompt sets.
[03:54] Jasmine: Also curious about autoscaling — will Dedicated handle spikes?
[04:00] Evan: Yes, Dedicated has autoscaling policies and burst options. We can configure target throughput and autoscale windows; for very spiky traffic we'll add buffer capacity or fallback to hosted variants.
[04:14] Dr. Aaron: Pricing — can you give a ballpark for Dedicated vs hosted?
[04:19] Maya: I'll send a preliminary pricing sheet. High-level: hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings), Dedicated has a monthly reserved capacity and predictable unit cost. We'll include example numbers for your expected throughput.
[04:34] Samir: For the private deployment, we need a runbook on kernel/quantization recommendations — we use 8-bit quantization in prod; will that be supported?
[04:46] Evan: Our runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and recommends kernels based on model architecture. There may be model-specific caveats; we'll run a short benchmark.
[04:57] Jordan: Quick note on support SLAs — we have a dedicated CSM and 24/7 support for enterprise tiers. We'll align SLA once we decide on Dedicated/Private.
[05:10] Dr. Aaron: Great. Let's talk pilot scope — what would success look like by the end of the pilot?
[05:18] Maya: Typically success criteria are: 1) successful integration with your auth and traffic flow, 2) performance within your latency SLOs for the main workflows, 3) security/compliance sign-off on logs and retention, and 4) a go/no-go decision on Dedicated or Private deployment.
[05:34] Leah: We'll add quality metrics — like precision/recall on the reranker and generation score across our eval set.
[05:40] Maya: Perfect — please send the eval criteria.
[05:44] Leah: Will do.
[05:48] [06:00] Jasmine: Operational question — who handles key rotations if we use customer-managed KMS?
[06:05] Evan: If you manage keys in your KMS and we integrate, key rotation is in your control. For Dedicated/Private we can support HSM/KMS integration to meet your rotation requirements.
[06:18] Dr. Aaron: Any nuance on KV cache or session passthrough for chat flows? We do long contexts.
[06:26] Evan: Our runtime manages KV cache and supports session-affinity. For very long contexts we recommend local prefix caching combined with server-side KV to reduce tokens and latency. We'll put together guidance tailored to your flows.
[06:44] Maya: OK, next steps recap — I'll share onboarding playbook and SOC 2 + security docs. Evan will prepare a VPC/private deployment doc and run a short benchmark on your sample prompts. Samir will share infra diagram and allowlist. Leah will share eval prompt sets.
[07:00] Jasmine: That sounds good. Can we set the deep technical call now?
[07:06] Maya: We suggested 2027-10-13 at 10:00 PT — is that okay for everyone?
[07:12] Samir: Works for me.
[07:14] Leah: Works.
[07:16] Dr. Aaron: Yes.
[07:18] Evan: I'll block the time and include a runbook agenda.
[07:22] [07:45] Dr. Aaron: One more security thing — we'd like to review your SOC 2 report; will you redact customer names?
[07:30] Maya: Yes, we can share a redacted SOC 2 and customer attestations. I'll attach it to the follow-up email.
[07:36] Jasmine: Onboarding timeline — what's typical for us to go from pilot to prod? We have a Q1 goal.
[07:42] Maya: With a pilot starting mid-October, and a couple of weeks for integration and a two-week validation window, conservative estimate is go-live in late December/early January — realistic for Q1. If you choose Dedicated/Private there is a provisioning lead time, but we'll coordinate.
[07:58] [09:00] Samir: Are there firewall/NAT traversal recommendations if we do hosted? Our strict posture may make hosted harder.
[09:09] Evan: We'll provide an IP allowlist and recommend TLS mutual auth for sensitive endpoints. For the strictest posture we recommend VPC peering or private link.
[09:22] Leah: Any pre-built SDKs for our frontend? We mostly use TypeScript React and Python for backend.
[09:28] Maya: We have official SDKs for TS and Python and sample React components. We'll share links.
[09:34] Jasmine: Great. Anything else from the team?
[09:37] Dr. Aaron: No, thanks.
[09:40] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll send the playbook and security pack today, Evan will follow up on the VPC doc and benchmark, Samir and Leah please send artifacts by 10/8.
[09:51] Jasmine: Thanks, bye.
[09:53] [48:00] Meeting ends
